plan.notes: Source: official College of Southern Idaho 2024-2025 catalog, 'Biology, Associate of Science' program page (Major Code: 1941S), hand-transcribed 2026-10-02 from https://csi.smartcatalogiq.com/en/2024-2025/2024-2025-catalog/biology-department/biology/biology-associate-of-science . Transcription method: fetched the official program page and transcribed the four 'Fall/Spring Semester Freshman/Sophomore Year' tables verbatim (course codes, titles, credits, printed semester totals). TRUE award: Associate of Science (page title 'Biology, Associate of Science'; the CSI majors index confirms the AS award). Catalog year 2024-2025: the newest CSI catalog with complete published program pages found (a 2025-2026 catalog exists but its program pages were not locatable; the 2024-2025 pages are complete and officially published). Total credits: 60, the catalog's published minimum ('Total Credit Hours: 60-65'). Semester tables print ranges (13-18 / 10-15) because Program Electives are 0-5 credits per semester with 5 total hours required ('Program Electives 5 hours' on the page). Modeled honestly per corpus convention: PROG ELEC as 3 SCH in semester 3 + 2 SCH in semester 4 (sums to the required 5; each within the official 0-5 range), giving semester totals 16 and 12 and plan total 60. Choice slots: 'BIOL 209 General Ecology OR BIOL 250 General Microbiology' (both 4 cr; catalog notes some transfer institutions may require both); COMM GE / HUMA GE / HUMA GE2 / SOCS GE / SOCS GE2 / WELL are official catalog placeholders for 'any Gen. Ed.' course in that category (student choice); PROG ELEC rows are 'Program Electives' (student choice from the program-electives list printed on the page). Prereqs: left empty. The catalog marks courses with '*' as 'Prerequisite or corequisite required' but does not name the prerequisite on the plan page; per-course prerequisites live on the official catalog course pages, not the plan page. The catalog notes 'Alternative plans of study available by contacting your advisor.' Footnotes: Social Science courses must be from 2 different disciplines; Humanities courses must be from 2 disciplines.
